definitions.explanation: A building with many stories, especially as a category. The 〜{建|だ}て suffix indicates how many stories a building has; {高層建|こうそうだ}て groups together all the tall ones.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{高層建|こうそうだ}て⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: High-rise buildings line the area in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{高層建|こうそうだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: A new high-rise apartment building went up in the neighborhood.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地震|じしん}→地震：01608_jishin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{高層建|こうそうだ}て⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{耐震|たいしん}→耐震：06222_taishin⟧⟦{基準|きじゅん}→基準：00228_kijun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{設|もう}けられている→設ける：14220_moukeru⟧。
examples.english: In earthquake-prone Japan, strict seismic standards apply to high-rises.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{高層|こうそう}→高層：04145_kousou⟧ (high-rise; many-storied) + the suffix {建|だ}て (number-of-stories building). Often interchangeable with {高層建物|こうそうたてもの} or ⟦{高層|こうそう}ビル→高層ビル：16994_kousoubiru⟧, depending on register.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高層建|こうそうだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧: high-rise condominium
- {高層建|こうそうだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧オフィスビル: high-rise office building
- {超|ちょう}{高層建|こうそうだ}て: super-tall / skyscraper-class

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{高層|こうそう}ビル→高層ビル：16994_kousoubiru⟧: high-rise building — more common in everyday speech
- ⟦タワーマンション→タワーマンション：28914_tawaamanshon⟧: tower-style condominium — specifically tall residential towers
- ⟦{平屋建|ひらやだ}て→平屋建て：28473_hirayadate⟧: single-story building — the 〜{建|だ}て counterpart at the other extreme
